description: City will conduct a by-election for School Division Ward 5.
By-election to fill a vacancy on October 28.

Modern Erratics Project installed three recycled material sculptures for $297,000.
Located at Material Recovery Center, Diefenbaker, and Forestry Farm Parks.
Council debated removing the public art funding policy.

chips.text: Saskatchewan arts and culture sector contributes over $1 billion to provincial GDP.
Councillor Donauer consistently opposed the 1% public art funding policy.
Local artists, fabricators, and contractors benefited from project investment.
Councillor Parker supported removing funding, citing resident concerns about sidewalk repairs.
Trade agreements prevent the city from requiring local procurement for art projects.
Waste reduction from recycled art contributes to avoiding $120M landfill cost.
Mayor Block signaled a motion to improve public art communication and funding avenues.

speakers.name: Tristan Surtees
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Public Art Policy and the Modern Erratics Project
said: Public art is economic investment, supporting local economy and jobs.
Modern Erratic project created economically with 5,500 hours of care.
Public art builds city strength, cultural heritage, asset.

speakers.name: Kelsey Ford
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Public Art Policy and Modern Erratics Project
said: Maintain 1% civic capital project public art funding stream.
Public art provides social, educational, cultural, economic, quality of life benefits.
City must improve communication and education about public art investments.

speakers.name: Daniel Macdonald
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: City's Public Art Policy
said: Opposes motion to eliminate capital arts funding.
Public art's first priority is to create public discussion.
Eliminating funding is wrong tool; removes money without creating other funds.

speakers.name: Jean-Sébastien Gauthier
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: City's Public Art Policy
said: Supports maintaining 1% for the Arts Policy as proven investment.
Public art creates business opportunities for local fabricators and workers.
Policy builds civic identity, artistic legacy, and strengthens technical capacity.

speakers.name: Stephanie Bellefleur
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: City's Public Art Policy
said: Has grave concerns about municipal systems supporting artists.
Advocates for championing, celebrating, and supporting artists in partnership.
Dismantling 1% system is disheartening; businesses should be accountable.

description: Councillor Donauer proposed removing public art funding from large capital projects.
The funding stream allocates up to 1% of projects over $5M.
This policy has funded few projects since 2015.

chips.text: Modern Erratic project cost $297,490, 0.79% of its $37.5M budget.
Councillor Donauer consistently opposed the 1% public art funding since 2014.
Local artists, fabricators, engineers, and contractors benefit from public art projects.
The 1% for art policy was adopted in 2015 following a 2011 culture plan.
Numerous public speakers, artists
Councillor Dueck supported the motion
City solicitor noted trade agreements prevent local procurement preference for art projects.
Public art provides accessible cultural experiences for young families and marginalized groups.
Modern Erratic project used recycled materials like grain bags, bottle caps, and shredded carts.

speakers.name: Em Ironstar
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Councillor R. Donauer - City's Public Art Policy
said: One controversial commission should not determine future of public art policy.
Public art contributes to character of public spaces, supports artists, builds city.
Maintain the 1% civic capital project public art funding stream.

speakers.name: Deneh’Cho Thompson
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Councillor R. Donauer - City's Public Art Policy
said: Motion to eliminate funding attacks core values of why I love this city.
Arts and culture sector adds billions to Canada's GDP, outperforms other sectors.
Saskatoon residents outspend other regions on culture, but funding is lowest.

speakers.name: John Penner
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Councillor R. Donauer - City's Public Art Policy
said: Motion to remove 1% for art is short-sighted, commensurate with other cities.
Public art is popular, stimulates discussion, not guided by personal taste.
Rely on professional jury and cultural experts to guide choices.

speakers.name: Jake Moore
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Councillor R. Donauer - City's Public Art Policy
said: Democracy is a creative experiment, requires participation, dialogue, courage.
Calling art 'three plastic rocks' is reductive, cultivates contempt, builds division.
Arts and culture contribute over $1 billion to GDP, 20,000 jobs in Saskatchewan.

speakers.name: Betsy Rosenwald
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Councillor R. Donauer - City's Public Art Policy
said: Eliminating funding would be a tragic mistake for arts community and city.
Public art pieces like 'Unfurled' and 'Stolen Sisters' grace our city.
Criticism of 'Modern Erratic' could be leveled at any artist seeking opportunities.

speakers.name: Bryn Rawlyk
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Councillor R. Donauer - City's Public Art Policy
said: Motion is a step backwards; public art brings visitors to the city.
Visitors from Montreal enjoyed walking around city and enjoying the art.
Suggests 1% of private capital construction could also fund arts.

speakers.name: Daniel Macdonald
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: City's Public Art Policy
said: Opposes motion to eliminate capital arts funding project.
Politicians attacking arts when they don't understand it is problematic.
Pushing this motion is scoring quick political points, not leadership.

speakers.name: Ella Dawn McGeough
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Councillor R. Donauer - City's Public Art Policy
said: Public art is integral to shaping, understanding, and experiencing shared places.
Criticism of artwork is legitimate, but not reason for wholesale abandonment.
For every dollar provincial funding, $13.70 economic output generated.

speakers.name: Jean-Sébastien Gauthier
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: City's Public Art Policy
said: Maintaining 1% for Arts Policy is proven investment in artists, industry, identity.
Public art creates business opportunities for local fabricators, contractors, designers.
Policy is not an accessory; it's an investment in Saskatoon's profile.

speakers.name: Stephanie Bellefleur
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: City's Public Art Policy
said: Grave concerns around municipal systems supporting artists, particularly public art.
Dismantling 1% system is disheartening; holding businesses accountable is necessary.
Need to understand art is broader, supports marginalized communities.

speakers.name: Andrew Keith
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Councillor R. Donauer - City's Public Art Policy
said: Art transcends time, produces culture, connection, human engagement.
City needs to fund art at a civic scale to create artist ecosystem.
Zero funding is not the answer; art persists and opinions change.
